title: Deployment Symphony: Calendar & Ops Checklist (May–Jun 2026) [WIP]
content:
Purpose
This is a working ops doc for the May→June 2026 feature bundle (internal name: deployment-symphony). Aim: provide a single living checklist + calendar for the release engineering team and EMs to coordinate cutover windows, canaries, rollbacks, and post-release validation.

Context / scope
- Contains changes affecting: serving-runtime kernels, routing layer, Dedicated autoscaler config, and minor Console UI toggles for rollout controls.
- Target audience: release engineers, SRE on-call, product EMs, platform QA.
- Expected risk profile: medium (kernel and routing touches). No DB schema changes.

High-level release cadence (summary)
- Week of May 18: Code freeze for runtime + infra (exceptions require REL owner sign-off).
- May 20–22: Integration smoke and performance canaries in staging.
- May 26–28: Canary rollout to 5% traffic in prod (region us-west1 only).
- June 2: Increment to 25% global (if canaries green).
- June 9: Full rollout (default traffic) pending automated QA and ops sign-off.

Release calendar (owners and hard windows)
- 2026-05-18 09:00–17:00 PDT: Feature branch cut + tag (owner: Priya). Blockers must be flagged in REL-452.
- 2026-05-20 10:00–14:00 PDT: Staging smoke run (owner: Maya). Run list: smoketest-suite v3.1, perf-window 1k concurrent sessions.
- 2026-05-22 08:00–12:00 PDT: Staging performance regression check (owner: Lars). Compare against baseline commit abf3c.
- 2026-05-26 01:00–04:00 PDT: Canary to 5% (us-west1) (owner: Diego). Monitoring watch and rollback window 3 hours.
- 2026-06-02 02:00–06:00 PDT: Increase to 25% (global staged) (owner: Sanjay). Watch for p50/p95 latency spikes, error budget burn.
- 2026-06-09 03:00–07:00 PDT: Full rollout (owner: Priya). Finalize release notes and lock console feature gates.

Pre-release checklist (must be completed before any prod change)
- [ ] Release branch created and signed: tag: rel/deployment-symphony/2026-05-26 (owner: Priya).
- [ ] All PRs merged and linked in REL epic. PRs: runtime#1242, autoscaler#811, console#207.
- [ ] Release notes draft ready and reviewed by PM (see section: Release notes draft).
- [ ] Rollback plan documented and tested (see Redo steps below).
- [ ] Runbooks updated: oncall README, kernel-fallback procedure, KV-cache flush steps.
- [ ] CI artifacts archived with checksums (s3://releases/candidate/2026-05-26/).
- [ ] Security scan completed and no critical findings (owner: security-team).

Staging tests (what to run)
- Functional: full regression smoke (smoketest-suite v3.1).
- Load: 1k concurrent synthetic users hitting chat and generate endpoints. Expect p95 < 450ms for small prompts.
- Long-tail: 30m soak with KV cache hot-path exercise.
- Regression: replay 50 recorded prompts from customer-critical set.
- Chaos: network flapping test for 10 minutes (optional; if green then good signal).

Canary rollout checklist (5% to 25% progression)
- Canary start checklist (prior to any traffic shift):
  - [ ] Canary images deployed to us-west1 pool.
  - [ ] Canary health endpoints returning 200 for /health/liveness and /health/ready.
  - [ ] Tracing enabled and routed to tracing-prod/canary.
  - [ ] Alert thresholds temporarily lowered for p95 and error-rate (operator: SRE).
  - [ ] Circuit-breaker and fallback model variants configured (config id: cb-2026-05).
- Monitoring to watch (first 3 hours critical):
  - Latency p50/p95/p99 by endpoint and model.
  - Error rate (5XX) and client errors (4XX burst patterns).
  - Traces with >500ms tail.
  - Token cost per request anomaly (sudden increase may signal caching misbehavior).
- Rollback triggers (examples):
  - 5xx rate sustained >0.3% for 15m AND above baseline by >3x.
  - p95 increase >30% and sustained for 10m.
  - Customer-facing flows failing for Top-10 customers.
- Rollback immediate steps (quick recovery):
  - [ ] Pause traffic ramp in Console (owner: Priya).
  - [ ] Shift routing back to previous model tag (runtime-serving: rel-2026-04-11).
  - [ ] Disable canary nodes in load balancer and scale down.
  - [ ] Open incident channel (#releases + #sre-oncall) and run RCA if needed.

Post-deployment validation (first 72 hours)
- Automated: run postdeploy-e2e (10 runs per hour) and check pass rate >= 98%.
- Manual: product PM smoke on top flows (account creation, simple chat, embedding retrieval).
- Data: validate metrics ingestion - no gaps in token metrics and tracing.
- Cost: quick cost delta check for the release window vs baseline day.
- Customer: contact top-5 commercial customers to confirm no regressions (owner: CS lead).

Rollback and remediation playbook (detailed steps)
- Full rollback (if canary fails catastrophically):
  - 1) Put system in maintenance mode (Console toggle) to prevent new sessions.
  - 2) Repoint routing to previous stable model variant and scale to baseline capacity.
  - 3) Run smoke tests on stable variant to validate system recovery.
  - 4) Re-enable normal traffic routing once p95/p99 stabilize.
  - 5) File incident and update REL epic with timeline and findings.

Release notes draft (summary for end users/internal)
- Title: May–Jun 2026: Deployment Symphony — routing, kernel optimizations, and autoscaler improvements
- Highlights:
  - Upgraded attention kernel selection to reduce p95 latency on long-context prompts by ~12% in internal perf tests.
  - Autoscaler changes to reduce cold start variance for Dedicated pools.
  - New routing policy flag to prefer lower-cost variants during non-critical workloads.
- Known issues:
  - Console: ephemeral UI lag when toggling rollout speed (intermittent).
  - Minor differences in token accounting for quantized variants (investigation ongoing).
- Breaking changes: none. Backwards compatible.
- Migration notes: customers with pinned model tags unaffected. Recommend customers using dynamic routing to test in staging.

Open questions / TODOs (please action)
- [ ] Confirm with security that autoscaler change doesn't alter KMS access patterns (Sanjay).
- [ ] Validate long-tail p99 for embedding workloads (Priya). Current perf runs focus on generation only.
- [ ] Decide whether to include the console feature gate in the initial 5% canary or enable it at 25%. Pros/cons discussed in slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/releases/C02ABC123.
- [ ] Add retention alert to catch overnight token-cost drift (Lars).

Postmortem template reminders (if failure)
- Timeline with second-level timestamps.
- What changed, what broke, RCA and corrective actions (owners and due dates).
- Ensure public-facing incident page if customer impact.

Appendix: quick commands and pointers
- Promote image: tools/release/promote --tag rel/deployment-symphony/2026-05-26 --env staging
- Canary rollback: tools/release/rollback --to-tag rel-2026-04-11 --reason "canary-failure"
- Staging perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/smoke/staging-perf
- Prod canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/canary/prod-canary

Notes to self
- Keep this doc as the single source for owners; update linked artifacts list as PRs/epics change.
- After June 9 full rollout, copy final checklist into confluence and mark this doc as archived.

Edits log (recent)

- 2026-05-07: added staging test matrix + owners (Lars)
- 2026-05-09: inserted rollback triggers and thresholds (Diego)
- 2026-05-12: updated calendar times and added post-deploy validation (Sanjay)
